text:
Maya (Support): Hey team, customer ACME reported a sudden jump in tail latency on the embeddings endpoint last night. They send large batched requests for indexing (bulk job ~40k rows in bursts) and are seeing a lot of 500s and long queuing times. Suspect dynamic batching + high max_batch_size + burst concurrency is saturating the coalescer and causing long tail spikes.

Devin (Infra): Can you paste the exact error they get and any coalescer/runtime logs? Also which model variant (quantized/FP16) are they on?

Maya (Support): Error in their client: "500 Internal Server Error - upstream timeout". They attached our embed response which shows intermittent "batch_coalesce_timeout" warnings followed by long queue delays. They are using model 'embed-large-v2' quantized. I pulled logs from the node that handled their requests (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-10T02:12:13.123Z] coalescer WARN: queued batch size 256 exceeds preferred 128, waiting for window to fill (window_ms=12)
[2026-03-10T02:12:13.136Z] coalescer INFO: flush batch size=240 latency=42ms
[2026-03-10T02:12:13.160Z] coalescer WARN: backpressure on shard gpu-3: inflight_batches=8 >= shard_max_inflight=8
[2026-03-10T02:12:14.310Z] runtime ERROR: request timeout after 15000ms -> upstream cancelled
[2026-03-10T02:12:14.311Z] metrics: batch_p95=890ms, request_p95=16200ms
```

Maya (Support): Their client config has per-request payloads grouped into 512-size client batches, then we coalesce server-side. Their batch policy: dynamic_batching: true, max_batch_size: 512 at client, but server preferred max is 128. Repro hint: they send many simultaneous chunked requests which makes coalescer produce very large batches and the shard inflight limit is reached, causing stalls.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Thanks. Two separate failure modes could be happening: 1) oversized batches are forcing long GPU execution times and queuing many requests behind a heavy batch; 2) shard inflight limit is throttling flushes, which can push latency above client timeout. We need exact request payload shape to test locally (dimensions, dtype). Also, did they ever get a dimension mismatch error?

Maya (Support): No dimension mismatch reported by customer; they only see timeouts and 500s. Sample payload (sanitized):

```
{
  "model": "embed-large-v2",
  "inputs": ["doc1 text...", "doc2 text...", ... up to 512 per client chunk],
  "truncate": false
}
```

Devin (Infra): Can you share the node config for the serving pool that handled ACME? I want to see max_batch_size, batch_window_ms, and shard_max_inflight.

Maya (Support): Copied from the node: 

```yaml
serving_pool:
  model: embed-large-v2
  batch_window_ms: 12
  server_max_batch: 256
  shard_max_inflight: 8
  kv_cache: enabled
  dynamic_batching: true
```

Devin (Infra): Aha. server_max_batch=256 + client-side 512 bursts can create oversubscription. The coalescer increases batch size to reduce per-token overhead which is good for throughput, but when shard_inflight hits 8, further flushes are blocked until GPU drains, causing requests to wait for the next free slot. That waiting + large batch exec time explains p95 tail > 15s.

Alejandro (Oncall): Ops-bot flagged repeated backpressure on gpu-3 during the ACME time window. ops-bot: "[alert] coalescer_backpressure: gpu-3 inflight=8 -> throttling"

ops-bot: @channel detected sustained coalescer backpressure on pool embed-large-v2 between 02:05-02:20 UTC, avg inflight=7.9, peak=8. Tripped service timeout 23 times.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Immediate mitigation options we can suggest to the customer while we investigate:
- Limit client-side chunking to <= server_max_batch (e.g., 128) or smaller.
- Reduce batch_window_ms to 6-8ms so coalescer flushes earlier and avoids huge batches during bursts.
- Temporarily lower shard_max_inflight to 6 to reduce concurrency and keep GPU latency bounded (tradeoff throughput).
- As a server-side quick patch, we can enforce a hard cap on coalesced batch size (coalescer_hard_cap=128) to prevent oversized batches.

Devin (Infra): I'll repro locally with a stress script that simulates many concurrent client chunks of 512 to replicate the backpressure. Sara, can you add a dev canary that enforces coalescer_hard_cap=128 so we can test impact on throughput/latency?

Sara (RuntimeEng): Doing it now. Repro steps I will use:
1) start a local serving instance with current production node config.
2) run 100 concurrent clients each sending 512 inputs with a 10ms inter-batch gap.
3) capture coalescer metrics, shard_inflight, and per-batch execution time.

Script snippet: 
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do
  (python3 stress_embed.py --batch-size 512 --sleep 0.01 &)
done
```

and the stress client sends payloads to: `POST /v1/embeddings` with `Content-Type: application/json`.

Sara (RuntimeEng): Canary deployed with coalescer_hard_cap=128 on a single node; initial results show p95 down from ~16s to ~800ms for the same load, throughput drops ~12% but tail latency improves drastically.

Maya (Support): Great. I'll relay the temporary workaround options to ACME: reduce client chunking to 128 or wait for our server-side cap roll. They need low tail latency more than absolute max throughput.

Alejandro (Oncall): I'll book a quick change window to push the hard cap to shared pool for the next 30 minutes as a canary across 10% of nodes and monitor. ops-bot: create incident ticket and runbook entry.

ops-bot: Incident #INC-20260310-142 created: "embeddings coalescer backpressure -> customer timeouts". Pager duties: Alejandro, Sara.

Devin (Infra): Post-mortem action items to avoid recurrence:
- add telemetry to correlate client_batch_size distribution with server_coalesced_batch_size per-customer
- enforce a safe upper bound (server-side) that ignores client chunking when causing backpressure
- provide API guidance on recommended client chunk sizes and a health header that returns current server_load to clients

Maya (Support): ACME accepted the workaround (reduce to 128) and verified their indexing job completed successfully after we applied canary cap. They reported median latency back to normal and no 500s.

Sara (RuntimeEng): I'll open a PR with the coalescer hard-cap default change + config flag and instrument the per-customer batch histogram for the console. Assigning to runtime-team for review.

Maya (Support): Thanks all — closing this thread after PR merges and canary verifies. I'll follow up in a day to confirm no regressions. :white_check_mark:
